acceptanceCriteria: Each metric has a deterministic definition over retained session data and a labelled benchmark with reported precision and recall.
Metrics are emitted only by evaluation commands and are never read by ranking or authority code paths (test-enforced).
Missing session data yields NOT_OBSERVED, not zero.
body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: Phoenix ships evaluators for user friction (corrections, retries, frustration), tool selection, tool invocation and tool-response handling, mostly LLM-judged. Corvint analogue, deterministic and local only: from agent session records compute re-reads of the same file, reads outside the planned set (the unplanned-reads ledger), retried commands, abandoned or reverted edits, and time to first relevant read. Use them as evaluation outputs to compare context packets (pairwise A/B arms for the same task, as in the multi-arm CEM trials), never as ranking, evidence or authority inputs (invariant 4; SOL-V0-001, SOL-V0-007, SOL-V0-010). Benchmark each metric against labelled sessions before trusting it, per the Phoenix rule that every built-in evaluator is benchmarked.
title: Deterministic agent-friction and tool-use metrics to evaluate whether a context packet helped
